## The question {.roomy-3 .vc}

::: {.hidden}
$$
\definecolor{deckB}{RGB}{31,78,121}
\definecolor{deckO}{RGB}{192,80,77}
\definecolor{deckG}{RGB}{46,125,91}
\definecolor{deckP}{RGB}{123,79,157}
\newcommand{\cB}[1]{{\color{deckB}{#1}}}
\newcommand{\cO}[1]{{\color{deckO}{#1}}}
\newcommand{\cG}[1]{{\color{deckG}{#1}}}
\newcommand{\cP}[1]{{\color{deckP}{#1}}}
$$
:::

- Does a short reminder before an exam raise the share who finish it?
- Unfinished exams cause most low scores in large courses.

::: {.takeaway}
Answer: yes, by about [x]{.hl-key} percentage points.
:::

::: {.notes}
**Purpose**: the question and the answer before anything else; a short talk has no time for suspense. (about 1.5 min)

**Script**: "One question today, and here is the answer up front. The rest of the talk shows where the number comes from."
:::

## Approach: compare sections with and without the reminder {.roomy-1 .vc}

$$
\text{finished}_{i} = \underbrace{\cB{\alpha}}_{\text{baseline rate}} + \underbrace{\cG{\beta}\,\text{reminder}_{i}}_{\text{effect of the reminder}} + \underbrace{\cP{\gamma}^{\top} x_{i}}_{\text{prior grades}} + \varepsilon_{i}
$$

::: {.research}
[Data]{.rlabel} one semester, students in sections that did or did not receive the reminder.

[Method]{.rlabel} linear probability model; standard errors clustered by section.

[Finding]{.rlabel} $\cG{\beta}$ is the number on the next slide.
:::

::: {.notes}
**Purpose**: one slide for the method: the model, what each term means, and what is estimated. (about 2 min)

**Script**: "The green term is the effect we care about. Prior grades enter so that we compare similar students."

**Cue**: point at the green brace when saying "effect".
:::

## What to take away {.roomy-3 .vc}

- A one-line reminder raised completion by about x points.
- The gain is concentrated among students who start late.

::: {.punchline}
Cheap to send, and it reaches the students who need it.
:::
